2609.29730.title: The Gold in Bias: Maturing the AI Design Process through Verification
2609.29730.paper_summary: Bias in AI systems is typically framed as a flaw to be minimized, yet it also serves as a critical indicator of underlying weaknesses in data, modeling assumptions, and system design. Existing approaches often treat bias as an isolated problem rather than as evidence that can strengthen verification and governance across the AI lifecycle. This paper aims to reconceptualize bias as a diagnostic tool that supports rigorous AI verification. We seek to develop a multidimensional framework to analyze bias, demonstrate how biases emerge in both Traditional and Generative AI, and provide a structured pathway for verification-driven mitigation. We present a multidimensional framework analyzing bias across four dimensions: origin sources, emergence points throughout the AI modeling lifecycle, technical and methodological causes, and validation approaches for detection and mitigation. Through a comprehensive typology spanning traditional and generative AI systems, we demonstrate how biases manifest and propagate across development stages. Our analysis encompasses 30 distinct bias types, 16 verification methods, and 20 countermeasures, providing an actionable roadmap for practitioners. We introduce a hierarchical evidence framework that distinguishes internal validity (mechanistic integrity of AI systems) from external validity (contextual reliability in deployment environments). The framework reveals how biases manifest and propagate across modeling stages, enabling systematic mapping between bias types, verification techniques, and effective countermeasures. The proposed evidence hierarchy clarifies how different verification strategies contribute to mechanistic integrity and contextual reliability. We advocate for ''Ethics by Design'' principles that integrate bias verification throughout the development lifecycle, enabling the construction of fairer, more robust, and trustworthy AI systems.
2609.29730.paper_summary_zh: AI 系統中的偏見通常被視為需要最小化的缺陷，但它同時也是數據、建模假設和系統設計中潛在弱點的重要指標。現有的方法往往將偏見視為一個孤立的問題，而不是作為可以加強 AI 生命週期中驗證和治理的證據。本文旨在重新概念化偏見，將其視為支持嚴謹 AI 驗證的診斷工具。我們希望開發一個多維框架來分析偏見，展示偏見如何在傳統 AI 和生成 AI 中出現，並提供一個結構化的驗證驅動減緩途徑。我們提出一個多維框架，分析偏見的四個維度：來源、在 AI 建模生命週期中的出現點、技術和方法論原因，以及檢測和減緩的驗證方法。通過涵蓋傳統和生成 AI 系統的綜合類型學，我們展示了偏見如何在開發階段中表現和傳播。我們的分析涵蓋了 30 種不同的偏見類型、16 種驗證方法和 20 種對策，為從業者提供了一個可行的路線圖。我們引入了一個分層證據框架，區分內部有效性（AI 系統的機械完整性）和外部有效性（部署環境中的上下文可靠性）。該框架揭示了偏見如何在建模階段中表現和傳播，從而實現偏見類型、驗證技術和有效對策之間的系統映射。所提出的證據層次清楚地說明了不同的驗證策略如何促進機械完整性和上下文可靠性。我們倡導“設計中的倫理”原則，將偏見驗證整合到開發生命週期中，從而促進更公平、更強健和更值得信賴的 AI 系統的構建。
